title: Network-isolation egress fails with HIER_NONE after the host accepts overlapping Tailscale routes
symptoms: Every CONNECT to an allowlisted API host fails with 503 TCP_TUNNEL:HIER_NONE and an empty server field (-:-) in network-isolation (topology) mode
The same workflow succeeds in host-access mode, or in isolation mode when no Tailscale step runs
Agent retries report 503 Service Unavailable from the model endpoint while the allowlist already contains the host
conditions: AWF runs with network isolation, so Squid egresses through the dual-homed awf-ext bridge and the host routing tables
A Tailscale step runs on the runner and accepts advertised subnet routes (--accept-routes), which add policy routes in table 52 consulted before the main table
One accepted subnet overlaps or covers the runner's default-gateway path, so Squid's own egress is routed into the tailnet interface and discarded
A policy denial (TCP_DENIED / 403) or an awf-net subnet collision (NET-006) is a different cause and does not match
The overlap mechanism comes from one reporter's analysis; only the routing-acceptance change below was validated
rootCause: In network-isolation mode AWF delegates egress to the host network stack and does not install or pin host policy routes. A Tailscale step that accepts advertised subnet routes inserts policy-routing entries ahead of the main table; when an accepted subnet overlaps the runner's own gateway path, Squid's outbound connections and name lookups leave through the tailnet interface and never reach the internet. The earlier theory that a non-portable resolver such as 168.63.129.16 was the sole cause was not sufficient: the resolver-filtering change was merged and later reverted, and the failure persisted until route acceptance was disabled. The mechanism rests on one reporter's investigation.

probe.command: ip rule show; ip route show table 52
probe.expect: A policy rule whose lookup is table 52 that precedes the main table, with routes that overlap the runner's default gateway subnet, indicates this cause. An absent table 52 or non-overlapping routes rules it out and points to NET-002 or NET-006. Both reads expose host routing only and no credentials, and no traffic is sent.

action: Before the AWF step, reconfigure Tailscale so it does not accept advertised subnet routes (for example tailscale up --reset --accept-routes=false) and do not configure an exit node; direct tailnet peer connectivity for private MCP servers was reported to keep working. If subnet routes are required, make sure none overlaps the runner gateway path or covers the default route, or use Tailscale userspace networking for private endpoints only. Keep the domain allowlist and DNS filtering unchanged, do not switch to a wildcard allowlist, and do not run AWF with extra host network capabilities to rewrite host routes. Report persistent HIER_NONE with redacted routing output instead of widening egress.
